key_insight: MinLA-guided interaction removal reduces QAOA circuit depth, while classical recovery improves sampled solutions on the original Max-Cut graph without additional QPU executions.
engineering_relevance: The workflow helps fit non-hardware-native Max-Cut instances within practical two-qubit depth budgets by trading quantum interactions for classical postprocessing.
method: Use a Minimum Linear Arrangement ordering to preferentially retain short-range graph interactions.
Run QAOA with the depth-reduced surrogate cost Hamiltonian.
Refine each sampled bitstring using signed-residue local search or bipartite-block optimization with exact conditional min-cut solves.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on ibm_kingston covered 120 non-hardware-native 6-regular and Erdős–Rényi graphs with 40, 60, and 100 vertices, reporting substantial two-qubit depth reductions and near-optimal recovered cuts.
watch_item: Monotonic recovery guarantees nondecreasing cut values, not global optimality; performance beyond the tested graph families and hardware remains unestablished.
paper_title: Max-Cut QAOA on Non-Hardware-Native Graphs via MinLA Surrogates and Configuration Recovery
